Senses.Explanation: The teaching-body is a corpus-defined body or person-shaped referent whose predicates vary across direct explanations rather than collapsing to an imported glossary formula. Chan records define it through a person enlarging the Way, originally present nature, formless responsiveness, activities, and deliberately concrete answers. Qianyan places three word explanations together: a robe displays the teaching and so is a "teaching-robe" (法衣); "a person can enlarge the Way, therefore it is called teaching-body" (人能宏道，故謂之法身); and being everywhere and clear is called the "teaching-eye" (法眼). Other records give deliberately different predicates. Weilin calls it "each person's originally present own nature" (當人本有之自性). Huanglong says, "the teaching-body has no form; responding to things, it manifests form" (法身無相。應物現形), then raises his whisk and calls that the teaching-body before laughing. Lishan answers the question with "a flower in the sky, a heat shimmer" (空華陽𦔨). Xiyuan Daan answers it by repeating that "all activities are the teaching-body's function" (一切施為，盡是法身用).
Senses.Note: The corpus does not reduce the word to one theoretical proposition. It asks about the teaching-body's function (法身用) and "the matter beyond the teaching-body" (法身向上事). The Old Venerables Record says "the teaching-body also has two kinds of illness" (法身亦有兩般病): reaching it while attachment to the standard remains, with one's own view still present and sitting at its side, is the first. Another raised saying states that "the teaching-body speaks" (法身說法). These predicates differ, but every witness still designates the same teaching-body rather than a second lexical referent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法身無相。應物現形。般若無知。隨緣即照。遂豎起拂子云。拂子豎起。謂之法身。豈不是應物現形。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huanglong Huinan, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huanglong Huinan (黃龍慧南禪師語錄), says the teaching-body has no form, then raises his whisk and calls the upright whisk the teaching-body responding to things and manifesting form.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫法身者，即當人本有之自性也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Weilin Daopei, in the Cloud-Mountain Assembly Record of Chan Master Weilin (為霖禪師雲山法會錄), defines the teaching-body as each person's originally present own nature.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衣以表法，故謂之法衣；人能宏道，故謂之法身；無處不遍、無處不明，故謂之法眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Qianyan Yuanzhang, in the Recorded Sayings of Master Qianyan (千巖和尚語錄), places teaching-robe, teaching-body, and teaching-eye together and says that a person can enlarge the Way, therefore it is called teaching-body.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。大眾且置。作麼生是法身。僧無對。師曰。汝問。我與汝道。僧問。如何是法身。師曰。空華陽𦦨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), the section on Lishan names him as asking what the teaching-body is, instructing the monk to put the question back to him, and answering 'a flower in the sky, a heat shimmer.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「一切施為，盡是法身用。如何是法身？」師云：「一切施為，盡是法身用。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Xiyuan Daan, in the Ancestral Hall Collection (祖堂集), answers a question about the teaching-body by repeating that all activities are the teaching-body's function.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問如何是法身曰法身無相
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jiashan Shanhui, in a case raised in the Linked-Pearls Collection of Verses on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集), answers the question 'what is the teaching-body?' with 'the teaching-body has no form.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 又法身亦有兩般病得到法身為法執不忘己見猶存坐在法身邊是一
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunmen Wenyan, in his room instructions in the Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), says the teaching-body has two kinds of illness and describes the first.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉：「法身說法，青青翠竹盡是法身，未是提綱拈掇時節。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunmen Wenyan, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen (雲門匡真禪師語錄), raises the saying that the teaching-body speaks and green bamboo is entirely the teaching-body, then says this is not yet the occasion for bringing it up.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫法身者理絕玄微，不墮是非之境，此是法身極則。如何是法身向上事？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shushan Kuangren, in the Ancestral Hall Collection (祖堂集), asks Daan about the matter beyond the teaching-body after stating a local account of its limit.
